project.name: libwebsockets
project.commit_note: ARVO metadata does not provide a vulnerable commit SHA. The line anchors below were resolved against the staged vulnerable source preserved in container `gt-arvo_48959-workspace`, which still contains the unfixed `blcount[MAX_BIT_LENGTH]` code shown in `patch.diff`.

bug_description.original: The vulnerability occurs in upng-gzip where temporary arrays used for Huffman decoding are incorrectly sized to 15, while the Huffman trees can have lengths of 19, 32, or 288. This mismatch in buffer sizes can lead to issues when processing larger trees.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 27-byte libFuzzer witness uses its last byte `0x20` to select `lws_api_test_gunzip`, then passes the first 26 bytes as a gzip stream into `lws_upng_inflate_data()`. That gzip payload reaches the dynamic-Huffman branch (`btype == 2`), fills the attacker-controlled literal/length code-length array `inf->bitlen`, and then calls `huffman_tree_create_lengths(&inf->ct, inf->bitlen)` from `_lws_upng_inflate_data` line 539 to build the 288-symbol literal/length tree. In `huffman_tree_create_lengths`, the local counter array is declared as `blcount[MAX_BIT_LENGTH]`, and `MAX_BIT_LENGTH` is 15, so the stack array has valid indices `0..14` even though the helper uses raw code lengths as direct indices and the literal/length tree allows bit length 15. The saved AddressSanitizer crash proves this witness reaches an iteration where `bitlen[bits] == 15`, so `blcount[bitlen[bits]]++` accesses `blcount[15]` one `unsigned int` past the stack buffer and triggers the reported stack-buffer-overflow at line 253. The fix resizes the temporary arrays to the worst-case tree size and adds an explicit bounds check before incrementing `blcount`.

source.description: First project-side statement that consumes the harness-selected gunzip bytes and installs them into the inflator context for subsequent gzip/deflate parsing.
source.value_from: The saved `poc` file is `1f 8b 08 01 20 20 20 20 20 20 15 ff ff b5 ff ff 00 00 01 03 01 93 ff 00 02 01 20`. `FuzzedDataProvider::ConsumeIntegralInRange<unsigned char>(0, 1)` pulls bytes from the end, so the final byte `0x20` yields `select == 0` and the harness enters `lws_api_test_gunzip()`. `ConsumeRandomLengthString()` then consumes the remaining 26 bytes from the front; because they contain no `0x5c` escape byte, it forwards them verbatim as the `buf,len` pair stored here.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The increment reads and writes one `unsigned int` past the `blcount` stack array when the attacker-controlled code length equals 15.
sink.note: The saved ASan report is `stack-buffer-overflow` at `huffman_tree_create_lengths` line 253 and identifies `blcount` as the overflowing stack object.

root_cause.description: Incorrect stack extent. `blcount` is declared with `MAX_BIT_LENGTH == 15`, so it has only 15 elements, but the helper later uses caller-supplied code lengths as direct indices and the literal/length tree built in this witness legitimately reaches the value 15. The fix enlarges `blcount` and adds an explicit `bitlen[bits] >= LWS_ARRAY_SIZE(blcount)` check before incrementing it.

tainted_value_origin.description: First attacker-derived parser state that commits execution to the vulnerable path. For the forwarded 26-byte gzip input, the first deflate byte `0x15` is interpreted LSB-first so this assignment produces `inf->btype == 2`, selecting dynamic Huffman tree construction.

parser_admitted.description: The gzip header is accepted and the first deflate block is decoded as `btype == 2`, so control enters `UPNS_ID_BL_GB_BTYPE_2`, the dynamic-Huffman parser that later calls `huffman_tree_create_lengths(&inf->ct, inf->bitlen)`.

evidence_limitations: The saved artifacts do not identify which literal/length symbol index held the value 15, nor whether that value was written by the direct `inf->bitlen[inf->i] = inf->code` path or by repeat expansion. The source-grounded fact needed for closure is narrower and witnessed by the crash: at line 253 some `bitlen[bits]` equals 15 before `blcount[bitlen[bits]]++` executes.

fine_trace.note: Source. `lws_upng_inflate_data()` stores the attacker-controlled gunzip buffer and its length in the inflator context. For the saved witness, the harness forwards the first 26 bytes of the file here after consuming the final byte `0x20` to choose `lws_api_test_gunzip()`.

After the gzip header, the first deflate payload byte of the forwarded buffer is `0x15`; read LSB-first, it yields `done == 1` and `btype == 2`. That dispatches the inflater into `UPNS_ID_BL_GB_BTYPE_2`, the only branch that builds attacker-supplied Huffman trees.

Dynamic-tree setup initializes the literal/length tree descriptor with `numcodes = 288` and `maxbitlen = 15`, the distance tree with `32/15`, and the code-length tree with `19/7`. The crashing witness later uses the literal/length descriptor `inf->ct`.

By the time this branch is taken, the `UPNS_ID_BL_GB_BTYPE_2d/2e` state machine has decoded the attacker-controlled dynamic-tree description into `inf->bitlen[]` and `inf->bitlenD[]`. The saved ASan caller frame at line 539 shows this witness reaches the literal/length-tree call `huffman_tree_create_lengths(&inf->ct, inf->bitlen)`, not the earlier `clct` call at line 524 or the later distance-tree call at line 543.

Root cause. `MAX_BIT_LENGTH` is 15, so `blcount` has valid indices `0..14`, but this helper later uses raw code-length values from the caller-supplied tree as direct indices. For the literal/length tree from step 3, `tree->maxbitlen` is also 15, so a 15-bit code reaches the one-past slot. The patch fixes this by enlarging `blcount` and rejecting out-of-range indices before incrementing it.

The counting loop iterates over all `tree->numcodes` code lengths of the literal/length tree (`288` in this call) and uses each attacker-controlled bit length as an array index. Because the saved ASan crash is one element past `blcount`, the witnessed call necessarily reaches an iteration where `bitlen[bits] == 15`.

Sink. With `bitlen[bits] == 15`, this increment reads and then writes `blcount[15]` one `unsigned int` past the 15-element stack array. AddressSanitizer reports a 4-byte READ at line 253 and names `blcount` as the overflowing object in the current stack frame.

format.name: libFuzzer-selected gzip stream
format.contract: The staged witness is the exact 27-byte file `1f 8b 08 01 20 20 20 20 20 20 15 ff ff b5 ff ff 00 00 01 03 01 93 ff 00 02 01 20`. `ConsumeIntegralInRange<unsigned char>(0, 1)` consumes the last byte `0x20` from the end and maps it to selector 0, so `lws_api_test_gunzip()` runs. `ConsumeRandomLengthString()` then consumes the remaining 26 bytes from the front without truncation because they contain no `0x5c`, and those 26 bytes form the gzip stream passed to `lws_upng_inflate_data()`. Its first deflate payload byte `0x15` yields `btype == 2`, and the dynamic-Huffman description eventually makes `huffman_tree_create_lengths(&inf->ct, inf->bitlen)` process a literal/length code-length value 15.
